opportunities.programme: SBIR/STTR Phase I (America's Seed Fund), general solicitation
opportunities.amount_text: Phase I up to $305,000 for 6 to 18 months, direct plus indirect. Phase II up to $1,250,000. Fast-Track up to $400,000 then up to $1,155,000. Up to $2.0 million per company overall.
opportunities.deadline_text: Project Pitch at any time; invitation needed before a full proposal. Full proposals due 4 March 2027 and 7 July 2027, then first Wednesday of November. NSF says pitch replies take about 1 to 2 months, so a pitch aimed at 4 March should go in by about early January (my arithmetic, not an NSF date).
opportunities.eligibility: US small business with not more than 500 employees including affiliates; PI primarily employed (at least 51 percent) by the company; PI at least one calendar month of effort per six months. Company eligibility for this specific firm was not assessed.
eligibility_open_questions: Is the company more than 50 percent directly owned and controlled by US citizens or permanent residents (NSF and DOE pages say at least 51 percent / at least 50 percent)? Not checked here.
Is the named principal investigator primarily employed (more than half time) by the company at award and throughout?
NSF's get-started page says 'At least 50%' US ownership and PI at least 20 hours a week; the solicitation says 51 percent employment. Which wording governs?
Only one proposal per company per deadline and at most two pitches per 12 months: which programme goes first?
NSF funds technology risk, not clinical studies; is a wearable ECG plus magnetic recorder pitched as sensor R&D acceptable to the programme director?
opportunities.match_required: None; voluntary committed cost sharing is prohibited.
opportunities.restrictions: All work in the United States. Subcontract ceiling as a share of budget was not stated on the page read; the SBA directive requires at least two-thirds of Phase I effort by the company.
opportunities.decision_time: Pitch reply about 1 to 2 months; funding decision about 6 months after full proposal (NSF get-started page).
opportunities.fit: Judgement: the broadest federal route for either programme because NSF does not solicit fixed topics and accepts pitches year-round.
opportunities.quote: up to $305,000 in R&D funding intended to support projects for 6-18 months.

rules.rule: The same work may not be paid for twice: a company must not accept SBIR/STTR or other federal funding for essentially equivalent work, and must certify this before award.
rules.citation: SBA SBIR/STTR Policy Directive (version posted on sbir.gov, May 2023), Program Funding Process
rules.quote: Essentially Equivalent Work must not be funded in the SBIR/STTR or other Federal Agency programs

rules.rule: A cost charged to one federal award cannot also be charged to, or counted as cost share for, another federally financed programme.
rules.quote: Not be included as a cost or used to meet cost sharing requirements of any other federally-financed program

rules.rule: A cost that belongs to one federal award cannot be moved to another award to cover a shortfall.
rules.quote: A cost allocable to a particular Federal award may not be charged to other Federal awards

rules.rule: Time records must cover all of a person's paid activity, never add up to more than 100 percent, and split the salary across awards when the person works on more than one. The same hour cannot be billed twice.
rules.citation: 2 CFR 200.430(g)(1)(iii) and (vi) (2025 annual edition on govinfo)
rules.quote: Reasonably reflect the total activity for which the employee is compensated

rules.rule: SBIR (all agencies): the principal investigator's primary employment must be with the small business.
rules.quote: the primary employment of the Principal Investigator/Project Manager must be with the SBC

rules.rule: NSF (SBIR and STTR): PI at least 51 percent employed by the company, and at least one calendar month of effort per six months of the award (three months per six for Fast-Track). One person can be PI on only one NSF proposal at a time.
rules.quote: Primary employment is defined as at least 51 percent employed by the small business.

rules.rule: NIH SBIR: PI primarily employed by the company at award and throughout. NIH STTR: PI may be employed by the company or the partner institution and must commit at least 10 percent effort.
rules.quote: Each PD/PI must commit a minimum of 10% effort to the project

rules.rule: DOE SBIR: PI primarily employed by the company at award. DOE STTR: PI may be primarily employed by the company or the partner research institution.
rules.citation: DOE SBIR/STTR application hub, eligibility criteria
rules.quote: The PI may be primarily employed by either the proposing small business OR the partnering non-profit research institution.

rules.rule: SBIR Phase I: the company must do at least two-thirds of the research effort. SBIR Phase II: at least one-half.
rules.citation: SBA SBIR/STTR Policy Directive, Eligibility 1.2; repeated in PA-27-100 and DOE eligibility page
rules.quote: For SBIR Phase I, a minimum of two-thirds of the research or analytical effort must be performed by the Awardee.

rules.rule: STTR Phase I and II: the company must do at least 40 percent and the single partner research institution at least 30 percent.
rules.quote: at least 40% of the research or analytical effort must be performed by the small business concern

rules.rule: NSF SBIR/STTR: no cost share; offering voluntary committed cost share is not allowed.
rules.quote: Inclusion of voluntary committed cost sharing is prohibited.

rules.rule: NIH SBIR and STTR parent notices: no cost share required.
rules.quote: This NOFO does not require cost sharing.

rules.rule: DOE SBIR/STTR: a later (third) Phase II needs matching cash from an outside investor, and SBIR/STTR money cannot be the match. Phase I cost share was not stated on the pages read.
rules.citation: DOE SBIR/STTR application hub, eligibility criteria
rules.quote: Any SBIR or STTR Phase I, II, or III funds from any federal agency.

rules.rule: Technical and business assistance: agencies may add up to $6,500 per year in Phase I and up to $50,000 per Phase II project (May 2023 directive; DOE's Phase I ceiling of $306,500 versus $300,000 matches). NIH says assistance funds may now also pay for cybersecurity and foreign-risk screening.
rules.quote: $6,500 of SBIR/STTR funds for the technical and business assistance

rules.rule: California routes: CalSEED lists no match; California Competes is a tax credit earned through jobs and investment; LACI charges an equity warrant instead of a match. CEC manufacturing grants' match rules were not read.
rules.quote: CalSEED grants of up to $700,000 are awarded to early-stage clean energy entrepreneurs.

rules.rule: Under the 2026 Act agencies must screen applicants for foreign security risk and will not let applicants fix a flagged risk before award; NIH also caps a company at nine SBIR/STTR applications per fiscal year. Statute text itself was not read (congress.gov blocked).
rules.quote: limiting each small business to nine SBIR/STTR applications in a fiscal year

rules.rule: Rule 506(b): no advertising or general solicitation; unlimited accredited investors and at most 35 non-accredited investors.
rules.citation: 17 CFR 230.506(b), as summarised by the SEC
rules.quote: no general solicitation or advertising to market the securities

rules.rule: Rule 506(c): public advertising is allowed, but every buyer must be an accredited investor and the company must take reasonable steps to verify that.
rules.citation: 17 CFR 230.506(c), as summarised by the SEC
rules.quote: reasonable steps to verify purchasers’ accredited investor status

rules.rule: Form D must be filed with the SEC within 15 days after the first sale; states may still require notice filings and fees; 'bad actor' disqualification applies.
rules.citation: 17 CFR 230.503, as summarised by the SEC (eCFR text of 230.503 and 230.506 was blocked by a redirect)
rules.quote: file a notice with the Commission on Form D within 15 days after the first sale

rules.rule: Cost share on one federal award may not be paid from another federal award (cross-referenced from 200.403(f); the text of 200.306(b) itself was not read today).
rules.quote: Not be included as a cost or used to meet cost sharing requirements of any other federally-financed program
